records.text: Owens said the CIA trafficked drugs and weapons throughout South America during the Iran-Contra affair.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This was the scandal when the American public got to learn that our CIA was actually trafficking drugs and weapons throughout South America.

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms Owens made a broad claim that the CIA trafficked both drugs and weapons throughout South America during Iran-Contra. Current official reviews support a narrower account: the CIA and other U.S. officials participated in the Iran arms operation and supported the Contras, while investigations documented drug trafficking by some Contra supporters and questions about U.S. officials' handling of those allegations. The Justice Department inspector general did not substantiate that the CIA itself operated the drug trafficking described. The statement therefore conflates documented arms activity and knowledge of Contra-linked trafficking with direct CIA drug trafficking, and also overstates the geography.

sources.title: Statement of DOJ Inspector General Michael R. Bromwich on the CIA-Contra Crack Cocaine Controversy
sources.relevance: The official DOJ review says Contra supporters engaged in drug trafficking but did not substantiate the main allegation of CIA protection or direct CIA connection asserted in the controversy.

sources.title: CIA Inspector General Report of Investigation: Allegations of Connections Between CIA and the Contras in Cocaine Trafficking to the United States, Volume II
sources.relevance: The declassified official review distinguishes the Iran arms sales and diversion of proceeds to the Contras from allegations of drug trafficking by Contra-associated people.

records.text: Owens said the Iran-Contra affair involved the CIA and Mossad trafficking weapons through South and Central America and, if Mossad's account is believed, Jeffrey Epstein participated by running weapons through South America.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: the Iran-Contra scandal was a trafficking scandal that involved our government, the CIA, of course, the Mossad. ... Jeffrey Epstein was involved in the Iran-Contra scandal. If the Mossad is to be believed, that's how they first brought him in, running weapons through South America.

verification.notes: Official investigations substantiate a U.S. national-security network that facilitated arms sales and Contra support. The reviewed authoritative record does not substantiate the statement’s added claims tying Mossad or Jeffrey Epstein to that operation, so the compound claim is only partly supported.

sources.title: Excerpts from the Tower Commission Report — American Presidency Project
sources.relevance: Primary official investigation documents the Iran-Contra arms and Contra-support operation.

sources.title: CIA Reading Room document on Iran-Contra arms network
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous archival material regarding the arms-support network.

records.text: Victor Marx told Corby Hall by text that he could have Hall killed and disappeared to a banana plantation in South America.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: So, you know, Victor (Victor Marx)'s response is, well, ... of course, don't do that. You know, the lawyers will always find a loophole. ... Okay. And the next message is, well, I can just have you disappeared. I can have you knocked off. ... I can have you knocked off. ... disappeared to a banana plantation in South America.

verification.notes: Hall publicly attributed this wording to a private text exchange. Searches found repetitions of Hall account but no released screenshot, message export, metadata, admission by Marx, or independent witness that establishes the message. Unable to verify beyond Hall allegation; lack of corroboration is not contradictory evidence.
